title: Rushdown through the 3D set, finisher wind-up
items: The Rushdown chase now runs through the actual 3D arena: the camera turns side-on and tears down the set's street, with stalls and lanterns streaming past at real scale. The combo and finisher play on that same street. Painted-only arenas keep the streaking backdrop.
Each card you throw is one hit, and it deals damage equal to its cost (0-cost cards deal 1). The finisher comes after them as its own extra hit.
Combo hits are slower and heavier: a wind-up, a short freeze on impact, then the next hit.
Finishers get a wind-up: time slows, the camera pushes in, element energy pulls in around your fighter with a glowing halo, then a flash and a ring burst into the finishing attack.

title: Rasetsu's Rushdown
items: Rasetsu's Rushdown combo has five new strikes: front kick, overhead slam, jumping slash (always lands from above the rival), spinning cleave and rising launch.
Her finisher is a single iai draw of her odachi, ending in a crimson cut across the screen.
Her art and odachi now match her design.
Rushdown finishers now also play the fighter's element burst, like other finishers.

title: Rushdown chase cutscene
items: Rushdown now cuts to a chase: the Rush hit knocks your rival off the screen, then your fighter sprints and dashes after them while the background tears past.
All 31 fighters have their own run and dash frames, with weapons held the way they fight.
Hana flies after her target on her esper power, hands in her pockets. Valka boosts in. Both hover with a glow in their own colour.
Speed lines are left-to-right only and only appear once the rival is knocked into the next scene.
Fighters keep their outline for the whole cutscene, and both fighters reappear properly when the Rushdown ends.

title: Kaede's Rushdown finisher, Rushdown demo in Training
items: Kaede's Rushdown now ends on her own finisher: a spin wind-up into a flaming spinning roundhouse, with a fire trail along the kick and a fireball on impact.
Training has a new ▶ Rushdown demo button: it plays your fighter's whole sequence (Launcher, a follow-up hit, the Rush card at Max Chain, 5 combo strikes and the finisher).
Fighters with the new strike art keep their Rushdown combos on the ground.

title: Rush cards for every fighter, Kaede's new Rushdown
items: Every fighter's Rush card now does something of its own: Burn, Bleed, Chill, Exposed, Guard break, double hits, card draw, Power, Counter, Strings, Overflow and more.
Lyra's Rush adds Encore (your next attack this turn hits twice), Gogogo's applies a status the rival doesn't have yet, and Jo's flips a coin for bonus damage.
Kaede's Rushdown combo now uses new paper-style strikes (left jab, low sweep, uppercut, roundhouse, spinning backfist) in a random order, ending on a flaming roundhouse finisher.
New effects library behind the scenes for upcoming attacks.

title: Super knockdowns, new Rasetsu paper art
items: Fighters knocked down by a super now lie flat on the ground in their own lying-down pose instead of falling over as a turned standing sprite. Nyx, Orin and Rei, who have no lying-down pose, drop to their kneel.
The fighter taking a super is drawn to the size chart, so a big fighter stays big and a small one stays small next to the attacker.
With paper sprites on, the fighter taking a super stays in paper form for the whole cinematic.
New paper sprite for Rasetsu, closer to her original look: odachi sheathed and held upright.

title: 3D free roam in the bracket, new roam NPCs
items: Free-roam stops in the bracket now open in 3D: the Moonlit Bamboo Road or the Neon Ward, walked as your run's fighter with your real HP and Mon. Walk off either end to head back.
NPCs are in the 3D zones: talk to them for heals, cards, conditions and deals.
12 new roam NPCs: Bruna, Maya, Nyx, Rhea, Azami, Varro, Lyra, Wukong, Rasetsu, Titan Mask, Akane and Hana, each with their own effect.
Mentors are rarer: about one roam visit in seven, at most once a run.
Fixed enemy art and portraits not loading in the 3D roam.

title: Health fixes
items: Bruna, Orin and Mirei had far too much health in runs after the last balance pass: Bruna 256 → 166, Orin 180 → 141, Mirei 218 → 150
Versus health is unchanged (Bruna 162, Mirei 152, Orin 141), and the Versus, Training and online character select now shows each fighter's real Versus health instead of their run health

title: Rushdown cinematic
items: Rushdown is now its own cinematic: the Rush hit blasts the rival off the field, then it cuts to a full-screen chase with after-images and heavy speed lines
You catch them, everything freezes into slow motion while you pick the cards to throw
Then an auto-combo plays out with the fighter's own attack moves, one hit per card: Flurry, Juggle, Phantom or Carry
On 3D stages the fight lands on the next stage over behind the closing flash
Fixed: both fighters disappearing after a Rushdown

title: Counter poses and fighters coming back
items: When you counter, your fighter now always swings into the foreground facing away from the camera, even against foes, bosses and mentors who have no counter art of their own

Fixed fighters sometimes staying invisible after an ult, super or critical (most often on 3D stages): the game now checks both fighters when a cinematic ends and at each turn, and puts back anyone left missing

title: Paper outline fixes
items: Group fights: the enemies waiting in the back line now use paper art and the paper outline too.
Fixed fighters losing their paper outline after taking hits (most noticeable after an Ultimate).
The next enemy stepping in during a group or wave fight keeps the paper look.

title: Online lobby picks, Google account sign-in
items: Online versus: make or join a room first, then choose your fighter and build inside the lobby. See your rival's pick live and press Ready; the match starts when both players are ready.
After an online match, Back to lobby lets both players change fighter or build without leaving the room.
New Account tab in Settings: sign in with Google to keep your progress across devices (switching on soon).

title: Bamboo Grove in 3D, scenery shadows on fighters
items: Bamboo Grove is now a full 3D stage: a rain-wet clearing walled in by bamboo, a misty pond with lanterns and blue spirit flames, mossy jizo, irises and streamer ropes. Every stage now has a 3D set
On 3D stages the scenery's shadows fall on the fighters: stand in the shade of bamboo, stalls or buildings and your fighter darkens
Fox Shrine Stairs and Bamboo Grove: the flagstone floor fades softly into the ground

title: Fox Shrine Stairs in 3D
items: Fox Shrine Stairs is now a full 3D stage at true scale: a stone landing at the foot of a long stair climbing through a tunnel of torii, lit stone lanterns, painted kitsune guardians, autumn maples, spider lilies and a shimenawa rope, with the shrine hall glowing at the top and the stage painting as the far sunset
A Rushdown on Fox Shrine Stairs carries the fight down to Festival Grounds

title: Loading on the VS screen
items: The VS screen now loads the whole fight before it starts: both fighters' sprites, poses, awakened and paper art, ult and signature cut-ins, mentor kit, card art, hit effects and voices

A loading bar in your fighter's colour sits under the VS screen; if the fight isn't ready when the VS screen ends, it waits (never more than 9 seconds), and anything left keeps loading behind the fight
Smoother first hits, supers and cut-ins, since their art is already decoded when they play

title: Mixed combos, paper border fix
items: Physical and spirit attacks now chain into the same combo; a Finisher cashes in any chain, and Rush reads it the same way
Paper mode: launched fighters, awakened forms and kneels keep the same border thickness as the base sprites
Fields: the field badge now shows the effect, whose field it is and the turns left

title: Slam words and impact frames
items: Counter results are now one big slanted word that punches in and drifts (DEFLECTED, PERFECT…) with a small COUNTER tag, instead of a boxed stamp
Finishers match: FINISH slams in and gets sliced in two along a white cut, tagged with the element and chain (e.g. FIRE ×3), in the finisher's element colour
Speed lines are gone from hits, dashes, camera punches and signature cut-ins; heavy hits now flash a two-frame black-and-white impact frame with ink spikes
Signature attacks play as a full-screen comic panel: halftone dots, ink border and manga lettering for the move name
Your hit counter no longer resets during your own turn from pauses like burn, shock, poison or bleed ticks; it only ends with your turn or a counter
Tick or thorns damage taken on your own turn no longer cuts off the attack animation you're in the middle of

title: Stronger shadows
items: On 3D stages the fighters' ground shadows are much darker and no longer wash out in fog
Fighters in the air still leave a lighter shadow, but it stays visible

title: New stage select
items: Stage select is now a fighting-game style carousel in the main menu's look: slanted stage tiles, region tabs (Bamboo, Festival, Marshes, Coast, Neon Ward, Boss) and both fighters shown up top
Pick the weather before the fight: Any sky, Clear, Rain, Fog or Snow
Arrows or swipe to browse, Q/E to change region, V to look around the stage in 3D, R for random
It remembers the last stage and weather you picked
On phones and upright screens, a grid of stage thumbnails sits under the main card for quick picks

title: Rush tweaks
items: Rushdown now also starts when your chain is already at Max Chain, not only on the hit that reaches it
A Rush card that would start a Rushdown right now glows with fire in your hand

title: Training mode
items: New Training mode on the main menu: pick your fighter, any fighter as the dummy, and a stage
The dummy never takes a turn, never counters and can't be knocked out; its HP refills each turn and its statuses still tick
Training bar: last and best turn damage, Reset dummy, Fill Spirit, +3 Energy, End training

title: True-scale 3D sets
items: Every 3D set now shows fighters at their real size: railings, fences, bar and stall counters sit around the waist instead of the knee, and trains, stalls and bridges no longer look like toys next to giants
Backup foes in group fights are drawn in to match the closer camera

title: Rush cards in the menus
items: Character select now shows each fighter's Launcher and Rush cards
The Codex lists every fighter's Launcher and Rush under Abilities

title: Versus loadouts and duel gimmicks
items: Versus loadout: pick a card pack (Brawler, Iron Wall, Tempo, Spirit, Fire, Bolt, Frost, Venom or Break) to fill your fighter's own cards out to a 30-card deck
Your fighter's own cards come in pairs (signature once), choose a mentor from the ones you've unlocked, and take a second insight on top of your fighter's own
Duel gimmicks: each Versus match can roll 1 of 15 rule twists (Sudden Death, Overclock, Titans, Glass Cannons and more), revealed with a slot-reel pop-up
The host can turn gimmicks on or off; online, both players get the same gimmick and a fresh one on rematch
Counter mode on 3D sets: fighters now stay planted on their ground spots while the camera swings over the shoulder, then pulls wider for the outcome

title: Rush and Rushdown
items: New attack type: Rush. Every fighter starts with a Rush card, a hit that knocks the rival back (onto the ground when they have a knockdown pose)

RUSHDOWN: when a Rush is the hit that reaches Max Chain on a rival you're juggling, they're blasted off-screen and you chase them down. Time slows and you have 4.2 seconds to throw cards from your hand: each one is a hit, stronger the more it costs. Thrown cards go to your discard pile
On 3D arenas the chase carries the fight into the neighbouring stage
Rivals can Rushdown you too, and it works in Online 1v1
Nyx, Orin and Rei now have launchers: Viper Ascent, Frost Pillar and Static Spring
Rush and Rushdown use placeholder animation and card art for now

title: Paper all the way through
items: Paper sprites now breathe in idle just like the classic sprites
In paper mode every form is a paper cut-out: attack frames, mentors dashing in, Rising Phoenix moves, super cinematics, counter poses, kneels and the awakened form
On 3D sets the stage light now falls over the paper sprites too: dappled shade and warm lantern rim, whatever pose they're in
Bamboo bridge: the camera comes in closer so fighters stand at their true size on the bridge instead of towering over it

title: Three more character themes
items: Wukong, Kuro and Akane each get a battle theme of their own: kung-fu action, a smoky jazz piece, and a fiery rock track

title: More music and background sound
items: Free roam now has background sound: waves on the Coast, stall chatter at the festival, busy night streets and howling rooftop wind in the Neon Ward, cicadas on the road and at the dojo, crows and a creek in the village, insects in the graves, crowd murmur in the teahouse and sake bar. It dips under roam fights
9 new character themes: Duelist, Azami, Kaede, Nyx, Rei, Rhea, Tetsu, Gozen and Uzume
An eighth track joins the random battle rotation
All music and ambience is credited in snd/MUSIC_CREDITS.txt

title: Kneels sized right, a proper train
items: Poise Break: fighters who drop to one knee now kneel at their real size instead of being stretched to full standing height (Kaiko, Orin, Nia, Wukong and others no longer look huge when downed)
Rush Hour (night): the express now runs all the way off screen before it comes back, and passes about every 25 seconds

title: Kuro's Ninth Life
items: If Kuro falls on his eighth life holding at least 2 Spirit bars, The Ninth Life wakes on its own: he rises at half HP already awakened

title: Online 1v1
items: Online versus (desktop launcher): Versus › Online 1v1. Create a room and send the five-letter code, or join a friend's room with theirs
Online fights are fully synced: you answer your rival's attacks in your own counter window, they answer yours, and either of you can call a rematch
Versus is now an even fight: no rival stat bonuses or fight modifiers, both sides start with 4 Energy, and fighter HP is evened out (big fighters still have more, but the gap is much smaller)
Hana's STOP. hauls the sign back, whips it overhead with afterimages and crashes into the rival with a freeze-frame, shockwave, clang and knockback
Bios show only the fighter's own height

title: New music
items: 20 new music tracks

Free roam now has music for each region: a festival theme, Tsugaru strings on the road, a haunting piano piece in the Willow graves, a travelling theme through the bamboo, a calm lighthouse theme on the Coast, and three tracks that rotate in the Neon Ward. The music changes as you cross between areas
New character themes for Rasetsu, Shura, Kaiko, Valka, Maximo and Hana
Four more fight tracks join the battle rotation, and journey bosses can now bring a shamisen-rock boss theme
Music credits are in snd/MUSIC_CREDITS.txt

title: Mentors join the fight, and paper sprites
items: Mentors now dash into the fight beside you and perform their technique with their own moves, then leave. Rival mentors come in from the other side

Four new mentors to meet in free roam: Old Genzo the Forgemaster and Karasu the Mountain Tengu on the Bamboo Road, Mama Koi the Neon Ward Fixer on the Neon streets and express, and Tamamo the Fox Priestess on the rooftops. Talk to one to unlock them for your next run

Paper sprites (test): every fighter redrawn in a bold new shonen style as paper cut-outs that sway on the stage. Switch between Classic and Paper in the fight menu (Esc), right under the Arena switch, or in Settings
Fixed: the red wound slash and elemental reactions played before an attack instead of after the hit
Fixed: the Shock effect showed a black box behind the lightning
Kaiko now has her bust on the map token
Settings no longer get cut off on narrow phone screens

title: Bigger codex cards
items: Meeting a new enemy shows a much bigger codex card, and their portrait now breaks out over the top of the frame instead of being cut off

title: Kaiju-sized, and a 2D/3D switch
items: Kaiko's KAIJU MODE is a real kaiju now: she grows to over twice her size when she awakens
New fit camera: when a fighter towers over the screen, the view pulls back to keep them in frame, in both 2D and 3D arenas
Giant enemies are drawn closer to their true size: Kuzuryu, Umibozu, the Gashadokuro, Orochi and friends loom over you
Arena switch: press Esc in a fight and flip between the painted 2D arena and the 3D set at the top of the menu, or press B

title: The Tournament Ring in 3D
items: The main tournament ring is now a full 3D arena when 3D sets are on: flagstone floor with the gold ring, packed lantern-lit stands, floodlights, bracket banners on stone pillars, flaming braziers and the judges' pagoda under a full moon

title: Kaiko, a connected world, and polished arenas
items: New fighter: Kaiko (KAIJU_KO), the Bedroom Kaiju — a fire and lightning zoner who builds Camp, with the AFK Barrage super

Free roam is now one connected world: 16 areas from Willow through the Moonlit Bamboo Road, Festival and Neon Ward to the Coast. Walk off an area's end to reach the next; signposts show where you're headed
Pick which region to start roaming in; every area has its own foes and loot, and each region ends with a guardian guarding a hoard
Arenas look sharper: soft glow on lanterns and neon, contact shadows, reflections on wet and glossy floors
Real 3D props with an anime finish across the arenas, plus painted extras: a commuter train, highway traffic, vending machines, food stalls, boats, willows and more
Floors get detail: cracks, moss, stains, scorch marks, manholes and litter
Holdline's floor is office tile now, and its bright office no longer washes out to white
Exam Hall and Canteen windows look out on a sunset town; Snack Bar shows the Neon Ward skyline; storm horizon at Calamity

title: Perfect counters get their rainbow back
items: Perfect counters bring back the rainbow trail: in slow motion your fighter dashes to the side on their dodge frame, leaving colour afterimages, then snaps back and strikes
The counter hit sound is back on Deflects and Perfects

title: Gunfire, cleaner counters
items: Valka's Rifle Burst now fires like a gun: she aims, and every shot has a muzzle flash at the barrel, a tracer, impact sparks, recoil and a gunshot sound
In the counter window, Take the Hit now sits in the middle of the screen right above your cards
Poise Break stars no longer hang around after a match ends or show up on the character select screen

title: Counter poses: the full roster
items: Akane, Hana and Uzume now have their counter poses, so every fighter has them
Akane counters with her katana still sheathed, swinging the closed scabbard
Akane's counters use blade slashes

title: Sunset Road in 3D
items: The festival road at dusk is now a full 3D set: cherry trees, lantern posts with banners, a canal and red bridge, and the colosseum glowing on the horizon. Every fight location is now 3D.

title: Every arena in 3D
items: Every fight location is now a fully built 3D set, 36 in all
New: Whalebone Shore, Lighthouse Point (with a sweeping beam), Cliffside Dojo, Watermill Stream (the wheel turns), the Snack Bar, Pachinko Parlour, Star Casino and Spider Roof
Boss arenas: Tama's room and its 3 a.m. Zoomies, the Landlord's corridor, the Calamity colosseum and the Reno site

Boss arenas change when the boss does: Weather's studio is torn open by a hurricane, Sun's shore catches fire, the express tears into Rush Hour's station, Proctor's hall turns red, Oba's kitchen boils over green, Kuzuryu's pool becomes a whirlpool, Holdline's office is pulled into a vortex, and Golf Dad's course is hit by a thunderstorm
Storms bring lightning, rain and flying debris

title: Counter poses for the roster
items: 25 more fighters now have their own counter poses: an over-the-shoulder ready, dodge and return strike, plus front-on swing, stagger and kneel
New: Bruna, Suzu, Nyx, Orin, Varro, Shura, Rasetsu, Maya, Rei, Azami, Maximo, Nia, Tetsu, Mirei, Lyra, Rhea, Shio, Gozen, the Duelist, Valka, Jo, Gogo, Wukong, Kuro and Ito
Nyx and Azami's counters now use blade slashes

title: Living 3D arenas
items: Six more arenas are full 3D sets: Neon Expressway, Willow Village, Willow Graves, Sake Bar Alley, the Neon Teahouse and the Neon Ward Rooftop
Every 3D arena now has its own painting as the far backdrop, so the horizon is never empty
Neon Expressway: cars, sports cars, vans and trucks race across the foreground, with pass-by sounds and the odd horn
People: shoppers browse the festival stalls, and pedestrians cross the Neon Ward street under umbrellas
Water moves now: ripples, reflections and rain rings
More detail everywhere: puddles, debris, petals and leaves, vending machines, bikes, signs, shrine lanterns, crates and more
City blocks fill the gaps between the near sets and the skylines

title: Counters, rebuilt
items: New counter screen: the rival's card up top with a live countdown, your answers fanned below with stamps showing what each one will do (Perfect, Deflect, Clash, Brace)

Every counter result now plays its own sequence: a late whiff on a miss, blows landing on your guard when you brace, both blows meeting on a clash, a parry when you deflect, and a slow-motion read and punish on a perfect
Perfect counters finish by type: Overpower breaks the blow head-on, Unravel slips it and cuts it apart, Phase lets it pass straight through
No more leftover effects: the cancelled attack no longer replays or shatters afterwards, and your strike back plays once
A cancelled attack no longer counts toward combos, finishers or Poise Break
Counter decisions and the timing rings run in real time, so Fast animations no longer shorten them
Keyboard: 1-9 picks an answer, Esc takes the hit, Space times the rings
Poise Break: stars now circle the fighter's head and they darken slightly; a launch takes priority over the kneel until they land
Fixed fighters sometimes vanishing after a counter pose

title: Three more 3D arenas
items: The Sunken Shrine is now a full 3D set: ruined stone gates, drowned pillars and the old hall standing in glowing water
The Mountain Pass is a snowy 3D set at sunset, with a rope bridge over the gorge, icicles over the cave and snow settling in the path
The Rooftop Terrace is a 3D balcony over a city of lit pagodas, with the colosseum and its searchlights on the hill

title: Real 3D arenas
items: Six arenas are now fully built 3D sets instead of a painting with depth: Festival Avenue, the Blight, Lotus Marsh, the Sea Cave, Pirate Harbor and Neon Ward Street
Real surfaces throughout: stone, planks, roof tiles, bark, rock and metal, all lit and wet where they should be
The Blight's lava runs through the seams of the flagstones and the Sea Cave's floor glows cyan through its cracks
Brighter night lighting on the new sets
Desktop: every save is also written to a file in the app's data folder, and the newer copy is restored at launch, so a run can't roll back to an old save (this needs the new installer)

title: Counters, reworked
items: Counters now cut to an over-the-shoulder shot: you see your fighter from behind and the attacker up the line. On 3D stages the set's camera swings with it
Four distinct results: Brace, Clash, Deflect and Perfect Counter, each with its own animation, hit-pause and layered sound
Winning the type matchup adds a finish: Overpower, Unravel or Phase
The counter window drains the colour from everything but the incoming attack, with a burning fuse timer and a heartbeat
Counter cards show the result you'll get before you pick
Poise Break drops the fighter to one knee with glowing cracks
New counter pose art for Kaede and Jin (more fighters coming)
Quieter hit effects; the spinning wheel, explosion, vortex and electric crackle effects are gone

title: Power-up auras
items: Powering up (gaining Power or getting Charged) now erupts the fighter's own element aura behind them
Fixed the awakening aura sometimes not showing the first time in a fight

title: Every location in 3D
items: Every fight location is now a 3D stage built from its own painting: the festival, harbor, Neon Ward, casino, mountain pass, every boss arena and more (47 in all), so the stage always matches where you are on the map
Stages come alive: lanterns and fires flicker, neon buzzes, the moon glows, rain ripples across wet floors and snow settles on the ground
Stage select in Versus: pick any stage, or View it full-screen in 3D first (flip through stages, try the weather). The 3D roam pause menu can set the fight stage too
The red bridge is now a long flat deck, and both fighters stand on it
Group fights: the crew lines up behind their boss on every stage and screen size
Fighters take the stage lighting in every pose, attack and awakened form
Launch hits go straight into the launch pose (no flinch frame first), and a knockout in the air falls from the air pose
New element auras erupt around a fighter when they awaken (two variations for each element), and soulscapes are off for now: awakening is aura only
Fixed the 2D map showing for a moment before the 3D stage, choppy 3D backgrounds during the talking camera, and square impact dust

title: Free roam shake-up
items: Free-roam areas pick different enemies every visit, with at most 2 per area (the guardian counts as one)
You can walk into a free-roam area without being jumped right away
Nue's fight poses are redrawn to match its original art
In the 3D arenas, awakening no longer flashes the 2D Soulscape backdrop

title: Bigger launches
items: Launched fighters fly higher, about half their height off the ground, and juggle hits pop them up a little more
Air strikes rise to meet a launched rival
Nia's Bookmark also adds 2 free Paper Cuts to your hand (they leave the deck once played)

title: Ito's new supers
items: Ito's Ultimate, Grand Guignol, is a full cinematic: she weaves a giant cat's-cradle web of red string, then it closes on the rival, hoists them into the air and cinches three times
Ito's Critical, Final Curtain, is a full cinematic: awakened Ito snips every string with giant scissors, the rival collapses like a puppet with its strings cut, and a curtain falls
New voice lines, art and sound for both
Ito now hovers when she moves, gliding on her strings with her feet off the ground (free roam and fights)
Shields have a lighter look: a thin glowing rim, with the hex pattern only flashing when a hit lands
Less flicker: the 3D arena is fully hidden between fights

title: Living 3D arenas
items: Supers now play out in the arena you are fighting in, 2D or 3D, instead of switching to a separate backdrop

The 3D bamboo arenas have weather (rain, fog, snow), drifting leaves and fireflies, and they react to the fight: hits flash light and kick up dust, and fire, ice, lightning and other elements leave marks on the ground
Group fights: backup enemies and summons stand on the stage, get the same lighting and shadows, and the camera pulls back so the whole crew fits. Very tall enemies pull the camera back too
The 3D camera now glides smoothly with the talking camera before fights
3D free roam: longer roads east and west, a real 3D red bridge, and new enemies, chests and pots along the way, with a gashadokuro boss at the end of the east road
Awakened fighters now sway in their idle like everyone else
Fixed fighters (and their counter ring) sometimes disappearing after an Ultimate

title: Snappier launches
items: Launchers now send the rival up right after a brief impact, instead of holding a long stunned flinch first
A launched fighter stays in the airborne pose when hit, with a quick spin, instead of dropping back to the flinch frame
Neon Ward enemy launchers (Wheelie Stomp, Hit and Run and others) now play the full launcher strike

title: 3D free roam
items: Free roam is now the 3D Moonlit Bamboo Road: pick a fighter, cross the red bridge, climb to the shrine. Strike first for an Ambush, every encounter is a real card fight on the 3D stage, then you're back on the road
Pots, chests, onigiri, an elixir, a technique scroll and the sealed offering behind the shrine guardian

Fixed: the screen could flicker or parts of it vanish after big cinematics with HD-2D stages on. The 3D stage now renders at a capped size, pauses under full-screen cinematics and frees its memory between fights
Fixed: a faint copy of the fighter could show beside them on HD-2D stages (the stage lighting now follows every move)
Settings → Display shows which graphics chip is drawing the game and whether GPU acceleration is on
Desktop app: always draws on the GPU (no quiet fallback to software rendering on blocklisted drivers) and picks the faster GPU on laptops that have two. Comes with the new installer

title: The voice update
items: About 1,570 missing voice lines are now recorded: the Neon Ward calamities and road enemies, Wukong and Gogo's full kits, and the new match-ups, each in the character's own voice
Every fighter has two new opening lines. Match-up lines now play about half the time; otherwise each side picks an opener and never repeats the one from the last fight
Subtitles now match what's spoken. Fixed rivals showing their old quote under a different intro line, card lines showing only the card name, and lines with no subtitle at all

Script pass: Kuro is no longer talked about like a dog, Sol is addressed as a woman, Hana's quote and several confusing or contradicting lines were rewritten and re-recorded, and reply lines no longer play before the line they answer
Fixed: pressing Back on fighter select after a fight now goes to the main menu instead of the finished fight
Desktop: the game window now remembers its size and position (needs the new installer)

title: Element finishers and new Kaede art
items: New finisher bursts for every element: fire, ice, shadow, lightning, steel, poison, blood, water, life, sound, wind and psychic, plus a white-gold burst for plain technique moves
Physical finishers burst in the card's element; Spirit Finishers burst in the fighter's element; enemy finishers play mirrored from their side
Free roam: a new 'New art' option under Kaede sprite in the pause menu gives Kaede a fully animated breathing idle (running and attacks keep the current frames for now)

title: Lit stages and win badges
items: Fixed: some rounds started with the arena grey and dim. A fight that ended during a counter window or a freeze effect left that filter on for the next round
Removed the coloured box glow behind the fighter whose turn it is (the red arrow still marks the turn; awakening glow is unchanged)
Win badges: every fighter you've won a run with shows a gold trophy on their tile, with a count after two or more wins

HD-2D stages: the camera now fits itself so both fighters stand on the stage's clearing at every screen size, with the set framed between them (lantern string on the road, torii and shrine hall at the shrine, the red bridge between two banks)
HD-2D stages: fighters pick up the stage's light (cool moonlight, warm lantern glow, drifting bamboo shade) and the moon casts their shadows onto the ground

title: Phones, tablets and a 3D test stage
items: New menu button on phones and tablets: Settings, Save, How to play, Run status, Fast animations and Rival turn ×2 are one tap away on every screen, no Escape key needed
Phones and tablets play in landscape (the Android app locks it; in a browser you're asked to turn the device)
Bigger tap targets on phones and tablets: buttons, chips, settings controls and the fighter roster meet touch-size guidelines
Dialogs like Settings scale up and scroll on small screens so the text is readable
Fighter select on phones: the roster is a two-row strip you swipe sideways
The Settings coin in the corner bar is now a gear
New test setting (Gameplay): HD-2D stages. Fights play in front of a 3D Moonlit Bamboo Road set that drifts, shakes on hits and sweeps on ultimates

title: Neon Ward polish
items: The Bosozoku Horn Kid now has his voice, and the Irezumi Dragon roars
The biker gang and the Pachinko Tsukumogami were redrawn: their rising-sun patterns are now flames, dragon crests and lucky sevens
Horde waves: a foe knocked out while launched no longer leaves its air pose over the next foe
The end-of-run Pass the torch screen now scrolls, so you can pick any technique from a big deck

title: Neon Ward
items: New region south of the festival: the Neon Ward, a rain-soaked Neo-Tokyo district that opens after the Semifinal. Reach it down the canal from Sake Alley, or by fast travel
Six new enemies: the Bosozoku biker gang (always rides as a crew of three), the Ghost Taxi, the Pachinko Tsukumogami and the Host Club Kitsune

Three bosses: Mama-san of the Snack Bar, the Oyabun with his living irezumi dragon, and the Neon Jorogumo at the top of the Web Tower. The Oyabun's teahouse opens once Mama-san vouches for you; the tower opens after the Oyabun, or by Ghost Train
Jo's high-stakes table at the Lucky Star Casino, mentor scenes on the Inari rooftop, a 24-hour konbini and an irezumi parlor that inks permanent buffs
New minigames: a UFO crane game and pachinko. Region events: Blackout, Neon Matsuri and Rent Day
Three free-roam stages (Neon Arcade Street, Shuto Expressway, Neon Rooftops), eight new fight backdrops and match-up lines between the new enemies and the whole cast

title: Stability & Quality of Life
items: Fixed: a fight could get stuck on screen after a K.O. that happened at the very start (bleed at low HP, or an Ambush that finished a weak foe)
New rule: no one can be knocked out by status effects or start-of-fight effects on turn 1. They hold at 1 HP
Fixed: Continue could reload a road or free-roam fight you had already finished
Fixed: choosing "Never mind" on a card pick (boss spoils, gifts, elite spoils, the vault) no longer hands you a card at random. You take nothing
Fixed: Copy result on the Daily challenge no longer claims it copied when the clipboard is blocked
New setting (Gameplay): Super Art cinematics, Full, First time per run, or Off
Fast animations now stays on between sessions
Full health now fills the whole health bar

Less flicker: impact frames, counters, crits and hit flashes no longer snap the whole screen to white or black for a frame, cut-ins fade out instead of popping, and menus no longer use a background blur that could flicker on high-resolution screens
Super Art cinematics fill the whole screen on every screen shape, and every fighter finishes their closing line before the fight returns
Cinematics fade smoothly back into the fight instead of cutting out
Every enemy and wanderer in free roam breathes with the same idle motion as the fighters
Fixed: some free-roam enemies could be invisible (only their shadow showed) until their art finished loading
Skip a Super Art cinematic with Space, Enter or Esc as well as a tap
Cinematics can no longer hang: they close themselves if anything goes wrong

title: Calamities, Size Chart & Fighter Bios
items: New Calamity: The Landlord, a grumpy building super. Rent is due every 3 turns; at half HP he starts Renovation and every wall comes down
New Calamity: Tama the Cat. She naps and can't be hurt. Wake her and she knocks cards out of your hand, then hits 3 AM Zoomies
Seven more Calamities: Golf Dad, the Exam Proctor, Rush Hour, the Weatherman, Lunch Lady Oba, the Customer Service Hold Line, plus two serious ones from Stage 3: the Unborn Sun and the Ninth Founder
Every character now shows at true relative size, in fights, supers and the codex. Kuzuryu looms, the Mochi Twins are snack-sized
Codex: new Fighters and Mentors tabs. Every bio now lists height, likes and dislikes
The Mochi Twins are now Mochi and Matcha. They call each other by name, and scream it when the other falls
All enemies and Nyx got flinch, launch and knockdown animations
New Calamity relics, keepsakes, and match-up lines with the whole cast

title: New Fight Stages
items: Mistveil Marsh: four new fight stages: Stilt Village, Whispering Bamboo, Mossy Graveyard and the Broken Waterwheel
Crimson Coast: three new fight stages: Cliffside Dojo, Lighthouse Point and the Whaling Village
Fights now take place on the stage for wherever you are on the map, and never on top of the map itself

title: New Ultimates
items: Cinematic Ultimate Arts for Kaede (Dynamic Blossom), Suzu (Raiko Rush), Rasetsu (Mountain Splitter) and Nia (Teacup Voyage), each with its own banner, voice lines and sound design
New Nia card, Storybook Summon: pulls a Rabbit Knight, Paper Dragon, Teacup Serpent or Big Bad Wolf out of her book to fight beside her
Her creature strikes for 2 plus its own status each time she plays a card; rivals can attack it, and recasting swaps in a new one

title: Cinematic Super Arts
items: 30 fighters' Lv1 Super Arts now play as full-screen animated cinematics with their own sound design and voice lines
New this update: Kuro, Lyra, Uzume, Shura, Rasetsu, Maya, Tetsu, the Duelist, Gogo, Ito and Wukong
Tap anywhere to skip a cinematic

title: The Launcher
items: Last Seed now opens into its own launcher with news, patch notes and one-click updates
Updates download only the files that changed, and resume if you close the launcher mid-download
Launcher settings: auto-update, repair game files, and hide/minimize/close while you play

title: PC Settings
items: New Settings menu (Esc): window mode, resolutions from 1280×720 to 4K and ultrawide, monitor picker
Frame rate: match your screen (120/144 Hz and up), cap at 30–240, or unlimited; optional FPS counter
Graphics, Audio, Gameplay and Controls tabs, plus Quit to desktop

title: 16 New Enemies
items: Horde: Lantern Bomber, Rat in a Coat, Rokurokubi Lookout, Door-Guard Oni, Empty Yoroi, Taiko War-Drummer
Road: Speed-Ramen Courier, Sumo Baby, Livestreamer, Obaa-chan, Kitsune Fortune Teller, Unbreakable Daruma, Street-Stall Chef, Karaoke Yurei
Minibosses: Kintaro Bear and the Lantern Bomber King
Every new enemy flinches, gets launched, tumbles and gets knocked down; the rats fall out of the coat when you hit it
